Hi Alex / Sierra — thanks for the clear questions. I wanted to give you concrete, actionable differences between Hosted (shared), Dedicated, and Private, and how we address noisy neighbors and SLO guarantees. Long but focused — happy to run through live on Wednesday.

Short answers up front:
- Hosted (shared API): optimized for cost and easy onboarding. Offers best-effort latency with standard rate limits and soft throttles. Not designed for strict isolation guarantees — p95 latency can vary depending on global load patterns. We provide per-request traces and token-level latency breakdowns, but we do not offer hard throughput reservations on the shared tier.
- Dedicated: provides capacity reservation (GPU pools) for your tenant only — compute isolation, priority scheduling, and reserved concurrency. This significantly reduces noisy-neighbor variability and lets you meet strict latency SLOs at predictable cost.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): full network and tenancy isolation; suitable when legal/compliance requires customer-managed network boundaries or on-prem storage.

Noisy-neighbor/Isolation mechanics (how Dedicated helps):
- Physical/resource isolation: Dedicated maps reserved GPU instances to your tenant (no sharing of GPU processes for inference).
- Priority scheduling: Dedicated requests are placed on priority lanes; other hosted traffic cannot preempt your reservation.
- KV/prefix cache partitioning: caches are tenant-aware so hot-prefix eviction from other tenants won't affect you.
- Network & disk isolation: Dedicated node pools have isolated networking (VPC peering options) and dedicated ephemeral storage for runtime caches.

SLOs and guarantees:
- Hosted (shared): we publish operational baselines (internal p50/p95/p99) but no SLA-backed latency guarantees for shared.
- Dedicated: SLA-backed availability and latency targets are available as part of a reserved capacity contract. Typical POC target we offer: p95 latency SLO commitments (example: p95 < 450ms for specific model + request size profile) with 99.9% availability on provisioned capacity. Exact numbers depend on model selection and sequence-length distribution — we’ll run a short calibration to confirm.
- Credits: SLA credits and remediation steps are documented in the Dedicated SLA (attached).

Observability & troubleshooting:
- Per-tenant traces, token-level latency breakdowns, per-route dashboards, and anomaly alerts.
- Request tagging: you can mark high-priority flows; those can be routed to reserved capacity or served with higher concurrency limits.
- Regression tooling: we integrate with your evals/prompts so any latency or quality regression can be traced to model/kernel changes or infra events.

Pilot / next steps we recommend:
1) 2-week Dedicated pilot with a small reserved pool (e.g., 1–2 GPUs depending on model) to validate p95 under realistic load. We run synthetic and replayed traffic from a post-call capture.
2) Calibration run: we profile model + sequence distribution to set the p95 target and confirm resource sizing.
3) Post-pilot: convert to monthly committed pool or adopt hybrid model (critical interactive flows routed to Dedicated; background/async to Hosted).

Attachments: Redwood_Dedicated_SLA.pdf (contractual terms), redwood_isolation_playbook.pdf (architecture & operational controls). I can share a short architecture diagram and a sample pilot plan in the follow-up doc.

Proposed time: Dec 2, 10:00am PT works — I’ll send an invite for 30 minutes and include a short agenda: 1) Calibrate goals (p95 targets), 2) Pilot scope & timeline, 3) Open Q&A on security/compliance.
